verdict.pair_reasons:
X vs Y: near-identical key coverage (both 23/25, both missing K17 and M7, both getting M6 only from session-loaded global instructions rather than from CLAUDE.global.md in the snapshot), and I found no material wrong claim in either. X wins on three specific verified findings Y lacks, all on brief items: (1) the denominator skew — `recycle-intent` is emitted at :12378 BEFORE inheritance at :12540 and `goal_requested` is computed from FIRE_GOAL at :870, so that row can never reflect an inherited goal (I verified :12378, :870, :12540); (2) the complete transport failure taxonomy — goal_unreachable (:801-806, body read) fires on exactly :7333/:7397/:7446 while pane-vanished (:7070-7079), never-reached-a-shell (:7081-7130) and relaunch-write-failed (:7187-7193) make no goal call at all, so an inherited goal disappears with no row; Y explicitly says "I did not read that function's body"; (3) the :862-864 comment claiming an 8th positional was deliberately not threaded is contradicted by $9 at :6945/:12628. Y's counter-advantages are real but thinner or off-target: the `.sentinel`-never-consulted precision and the empty-condition drop at :5846 are good, but several of its extra stale-citation rows (:9678-9686 account charging, :12729 self-close twin, :11232/:11237) audit machinery outside "this machinery," even though every one of them checked out exactly.

X vs Z: Z has the better citation audit and the better key coverage on that one axis — it is the only output that actually opened CLAUDE.global.md:223, hooks/goal-inert-watch.sh:36, docs/plans/NONLIMIT_RESUME_LADDER.md:753 and the two research docs in the snapshot, and every entry in its table resolved exactly when I checked it (K17, M7, and M6 in full — three key items X lacks). X wins anyway on accuracy and on the enumerated brief items. Z gets brief item 1's "name the store" wrong: it says the predecessor's identity is read "off its own live process, not off a stored pointer" and calls `sessions/<pid>.json` "its transcript file," omitting the PRIMARY source entirely — the `"session_id"` grep of `$CC_REGISTRY_DIR/<pane>.json` at :4959-4962, which returns at :4962 on the hot path; X states both sources correctly. Z also declines to check `set -euo pipefail` (it is at :343, and the brief demanded code-grounded claims), which leaves its brief-item-2 mechanism muddled; misses `check_goal_arm || exit 1` at :9015, so it cannot state the abort-vs-drop asymmetry brief item 6 turns on; misses the `shell`-arm early return at :12446 and the dry-run non-reach at :12787, both answers to brief item 7; and misses that resume mode clears even an explicit --goal. Against Z's three unique key items, X carries one key-item correctness advantage plus roughly eight verified on-brief insights and a 14-row in-file staleness audit with no material error. A false belief about an enumerated item outweighs an absence that X flags explicitly.

Y vs Z: the same shape as X vs Z and decided the same way. Y states the cc_sid_for_pane store correctly (registry row at :4959-4962, `kill -0`/ITERM_SESSION_ID/sessionId fallback at :4984-4995), cites :343 for pipefail, locates :9015, catches the `shell`-arm skip at :12441-12446 and the dry-run branch at :12787, and notes that resume clears an explicit --goal — five things Z misses or gets wrong, four of them directly answering enumerated brief items. Z's edge is K17/M7/M6-full plus the tests/handoff-goal-arm.bats:45 pattern-extraction observation, which is genuine and unique. Y's 15-row in-file staleness table (every row verified) is the closest thing either X or Y has to Z's external audit, and combined with Y's clean accuracy record it is enough.
